additionalCoursework: Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine does not require applicants to have taken any specific prerequisite courses. The Premedical Coursework is only recommended, not required. Successful applicants have a broad, strong academic background in life sciences, physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities as reflected in Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) scores.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Guided by Mayo Clinic's values, At Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine (MCASOM), we are dedicated to fostering a diverse, vibrant, and fully inclusive learning environment that embraces a deep regard for the vastness of the human lived experience and a genuine appreciation of differences, including ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, geographic/cultural perspective, veteran status, and socio-economic history and status.   

Our goal is to ensure that all students, faculty, and staff can achieve and contribute to their fullest potential while serving patients, families, learners, and one another with respect, concern, courtesy, and responsiveness. Inclusion is a core element for successfully achieving a broad community that nurtures, supports, and respects the individuality and contributions of everyone, encouraging engagement and connection throughout the institution.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Mayo Medical School has three types leaves of absence (LOA): 1) Medical Leave of Absence: A student may request a leave of absence for medical reasons if the request is supported by documentation from a health care provider. 2) Personal Leave of Absence: A student may request a leave of absence for personal reasons. 3) Academic Leave of Absence: A student may request an academic leave of absence to pursue a complementary academic enrichment experience, including a research program. All LOAs must be approved by the Dean of Academic and/or Student Affairs depending on the type of LOA.

MN Campus: Rochester, MN is a friendly city of over 100,000 with a vibrant economy, affordable housing, excellent schools, miles of hiking/biking trails, cultural amenities and unparalleled opportunities for medical education.

AZ Campus: Scottsdale/Phoenix is one of the nation's largest, most diverse metro areas and offers residents a vibrant mix of culinary hot spots, arts and entertainment, professional and collegiate sports teams and community resources. The region’s desert climate promotes an outdoor lifestyle with a full complement of sports and recreation. 

FL Campus: Jacksonville is an expansive city with 90 miles of beaches along the Atlantic Ocean. It’s Florida’s “youngest city” with amenities that include a vibrant arts scene, fun family activities, professional sports, jazz festivals and great weather that averages over 270 days of sunshine each year!

medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
We recognize the strenuous nature of medical school and the importance of making sure our students are healthy and maintaining a great work-life balance. We intentionally foster a supportive environment designed to help you thrive. Built into our curriculum and supported outside the classroom as well, we prioritize mentorship, student wellness, and overall well-being. We provide several wellness resources and encourage self-care and healthy behavior throughout your time at Mayo Clinic.

Among the many student support resources spanning all areas of well-being and numerous initiatives aimed at promoting wellness, there are a few that remain student favorites. One example is the Student-initiated Wellness Activity grant program that offers financial support to students who want to organize their own wellness events. In the past, some have used this grant to start a kickball league, while others have used it for a painting night.

Visit: https://college.mayo.edu/academics/mayo-clinic-alix-school-of-medicine/md-program/student-life/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine fosters a collaborative, inclusive, and supportive campus culture centered on patient care and service. Rooted in Mayo Clinic's mission, MCASOM emphasizes empathy, compassion, and teamwork, preparing students for multidisciplinary healthcare. MCASOM promotes belonging and inclusion through its curriculum and leadership, creating a welcoming environment for students of all backgrounds. With access to Mayo Clinic's resources, students engage in groundbreaking research and innovation while contributing to medical advancements. Community engagement is encouraged through service-learning opportunities and global health initiatives. MCASOM prioritizes wellness, offering mental health resources and work-life balance programs. Despite being spread across campuses, MCASOM ensures a unified experience through shared values and cross-campus interactions. Faculty mentorship and small classes provide personalized guidance for success.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional attire is expected during all patient care activities in the clinic and hospitals. The Mayo Clinic institutional dress code applies to students at all times.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: MCASOM has a student run peer-tutoring service with both one-on-one academic assistance and small group review sessions. Faculty and administration have office hours available to meet with students.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interaction within the first weeks of medical school and continue throughout the curriculum, reinforcing skills and bedside manner.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: During pre-clerskship, block style. Lectures are thematically reinforced during clinical integration sessions with patients, small groups, or in sessions with faculty.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Rotations begin after pre-clerkship curriculum. Students participate in eight core clerkships (IM, Peds, Surg, OB/GYN, Neuro, Fam Med, Psych, EM), a sub-internship, and numerous clinical electives.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Many lectures are recorded. Attendance is mandatory for major exams, Sim Center activities, direct observations, and patient and clinical experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Pre-Clerkship
You will begin the first 18 months of medical school in the Pre-Clerkship Phase, which focuses on establishing foundational medical knowledge. During this phase, you will also have the opportunity to utilize dedicated enrichment weeks for career exploration, scholarship, or additional degree/certificate programs. The primary academic focus of the first six blocks is the foundational sciences. Faculty combine didactic lectures with active learning to deliver engaging content in human structure and the principles of disease. After you complete the foundational sciences, advanced content is then explored, organized primarily by organ system. Emphasis is placed on developing and honing your clinical skills beginning immediately. Longitudinal clinical skills courses teach basic principles of interviewing, history taking, and physical examination. You will develop a clinical foundation, acquire skills of observation and physical diagnosis, and attain the foundational skills needed to enter the Clerkship phase of the curriculum.

Clerkship
The Clerkship phase spans the second 18 months of medical school and includes eight core clinical clerkships: Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Neurology, Ob/Gyn, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, and Surgery. Our commitment to improving the public's health is made explicit to rigorously inform the advanced students' learning experiences.

Post-Clerkship
The Post-Clerkship phase encompasses the final 12 months of medical school. The curriculum is composed of subinternships, electives, social medicine, transition to residency, health systems science, and internship boot camp. Clinical electives can be completed at Mayo Clinic campuses in Minnesota, Arizona, or Florida, as well as at national and international locations. Many students complete an international or underserved population clinical elective in the fourth year.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: MCASOM is committed to supporting all student interests, including those committed to a career in primary care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Mayo Clinic physicians and scientists have a long history of achievement in the areas of basic and translational research, including a Nobel Prize for the development of cortisone. Mayo medical students have ready access to Mayo's extensive research resources, more than four million medical histories and several well-staffed research core facilities on the Minnesota, Arizona and Florida campuses. As a national medical school, Mayo medical students can conduct research across campuses. More research information can be found here: https://www.mayo.edu/research
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students participate in clinics serving undeserved communities in Arizona, Florida, and Minnesota.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Mandatory research requirement. Research can be conducted based on individual student schedules throughout their four years. Expectation to have one publication by year 4.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine (MCASOM) is a national medical school unified by a single, innovative curriculum and educational opportunities across three unique campuses in Arizona, Florida, and Minnesota. As an integral part of Mayo Clinic, the world's first and largest group practice ranked #1 in more specialties than any other hospital in the nation (US News & World Report), MCASOM students learn from renowned medical experts providing specialty care to nearly 1.3 million patients per year. By partnering on bold national initiatives, MCASOM has redefined medical education through a transformative educational model that includes innovative learning and the flexibility to create unique educational pathways.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission: Develop a diverse community of servant physician leaders by providing excellence in education, fostering a culture of patient-centered care, and stimulating scientific discovery. We aim to promote health equity and improve clinical care through innovation and collaboration.

Vision: Transform healthcare through excellence in education, innovation, and leadership.

Core Principals: Lead, Transform and Heal

Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine will:
- Enroll an outstanding and diverse student body that has a strong foundation in the sciences and a demonstrated commitment to service and continuous learning.
- Attract and sustain an outstanding and diverse faculty who contribute to education scholarship and utilize the best principles of education to optimize students' professional development.
- Provide a learner-centered curriculum that aligns with evolving technological trends and integrates strong basic sciences, ethical principles, professional standards and outstanding clinical training.
- Provide an intellectually stimulating environment where small class size and a large faculty of physicians, scientists and other health professionals unite to promote the scientific and humanitarian practice of medicine.

In order to graduate physicians who will:
- Provide service and demonstrate leadership within health care systems and within the community.
- Serve as leaders of change to improve the health care system and delivery.
- Advance the scientific foundations of medicine through leadership in basic, clinical and translational research.
- Promote the role of the physician as educator-mentor and the importance of lifelong learning.
- Foster resilience and wellness in themselves and others, demonstrating work-life integration and compassionate self-care and care of others.
- Make altruistic career choices based on personal skills without the burden of excessive educational debt.
- Have mastered the knowledge and skills required for diagnosis, patient management, health promotion, disease prevention and high-value health care.
- Respect the importance of the patient as an individual as well as the needs of populations, and consistently practice evidence-based medicine and shared decision-making.
- Work collaboratively within multidisciplinary health care teams.
- Contribute to a diverse and culturally competent workforce.
- Practice both the art and science of medicine, and incorporate the highest ethical principles into their lives and practices.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: 10 business days before April 30. 5 business days after April 30. Two business days within one month of orientation. Subject to change.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine requires three valid letters of recommendation or one composite letter from a premedical committee. A letter is considered valid if it is on official letterhead and contains the handwritten signature of the letter writer. A maximum of 10 letters are accepted.

Once your secondary application is submitted and the minimum number of letters is met, your application will be queued for review and interview decision. If you have more letters than the minimum and you want them to be reviewed, we recommend waiting until your letters are in to submit your secondary application. All formal letters must be submitted through AMCAS. Letters added to your application after your application is considered complete, are not guaranteed to be reviewed.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
• We recommend at least one letter to be written by a professor in the life sciences or physical sciences. A letter from a teaching assistant is also acceptable. 
• Examples of letters writers include: research mentors, employers, volunteer supervisors, physicians with whom you have worked or shadowed, teachers and professors, and other professionals.
• Letters should be written by people who know you well and whose opinions convey the likelihood of your success in medical school. 
• Letters from family and friends are not accepted.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Depending on an applicant’s selection and rank of campus track in the secondary application, you could be invited to interview with any of our three campuses. Applicants who select more than one campus track option will only be invited to interview with one campus, taking into consideration the specific rank of preference. That interview will count for the other campus tracks that were selected.

Applicants invited to interview with us will participate in: virtual welcome session, two, one-on-one, 30-minute, virtual interviews, a virtual tour of campus, connecting with current students, and question-and-answer sessions.

Applicants should be dressed in business professional attire for their interviews.

Applicants will also be required to meet with one member of MCASOM's alumni network as part of our Alumni Visit Program. These conversations provide applicants with an opportunity to learn more about MCASOM, Mayo Clinic’s culture and values, and the experiences of our alumni.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invitations for interviews will begin being sent in August 2026.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Each interviewee will have two, virtual, one-on-one, partially blinded, 30-minute interviews with members of our admissions aommittee.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Applicants will be eligible to interview with the Arizona, Florida, or Minnesota campus based on their secondary application campus track preference. We do not offer regional interviews off campus.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: The interview format will be virtual, live video interviews.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
All applications submitted to AMCAS must include the following:
• Online AMCAS application - Submit the application from June 1 to October 1. 
• Transcripts - Transcripts for all previously completed academic programs must be submitted to AMCAS by October 15. 
• Application processing/secondary fee - Applicants selected for secondary review will be required to pay a $120 processing fee unless granted a fee waiver by AMCAS, for further consideration, by October 15. 
• Letters of recommendation - Three individual letters or one committee letter are the minimum number required. Review Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine letters of recommendation requirements and submit letters of recommendation through the AMCAS Letter Service by October 15.
• MCAT – Applicants must have completed at least one MCAT examination within three years of their intended matriculation and achieved a minimum score as shown on our website. Once this requirement is met, the admissions committee considers the applicant’s highest MCAT score as part of MCASOM's mission aligned selection, regardless of when that score was earned.

Primary application
As a national medical school, Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine has one AMCAS application for our three campuses in Arizona, Florida, and Minnesota.

Secondary application
Applicants invited to complete a secondary application will have the opportunity to select and rank up to four campus track options and must select at least one. Options ranked will be considered at the time of interview invitation and acceptance. *Do not select an option that you would not want to be accepted to. Select "Not Interested" for those options.
• Arizona 4-Year Track - The Arizona campus is your home base for all four years.
• Minnesota 4-Year Track - The Minnesota campus is your home base for all four years.
• Arizona/Florida Track - You complete preclinical coursework on the Arizona campus and then clinical clerkships on the Florida campus.
• Minnesota/Florida Track - You complete preclinical coursework on the Minnesota campus and then clinical clerkships on the Florida campus.

Acceptance, alternate list, and rejections
We make acceptance decisions when all interviews are complete and when our admissions committees have deliberated on all applicants. Initial offers of acceptance will typically be made in February. The Admissions Executive Committee could consider all campus track options that an applicant indicated on their secondary application at the time of acceptance, regardless of where they interviewed. *Do not select an option that you would not want to be accepted to.

Alternate list notifications will be sent once initial offers of acceptance have been communicated. Acceptances from the alternate list may be extended between March and June. Initial rejections will follow alternate list notifications and be sent at the end of the cycle.

medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept all coursework from an accredited college of university in the United State or Canada. This coursework must be provided on official school transcripts.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We encourage applicants to stay connected with us throughout the admissions cycle. After interviewing, you can submit an update letter, letter of interest (top three schools), or letter of intent (top choice) through the admissions portal. Even though you may not have all the information needed to make a final decision, we appreciate receiving whatever update you feel comfortable providing on your current level of interest in our program. No communication signals to our admissions committee that you are not interested in our school anymore. These letters are not a binding commitment, but a way to let us know your post-interview thoughts about our school.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
We understand the financial burden of continuing your education and obtaining your M.D. degree and strive to create a student experience you won’t find elsewhere at an unbeatable value.

Our goals are to:
•	Thoughtfully plan and allocate benefactor dollars to pass along value to students.
•	Increase access to the medical profession for all prospective students regardless of their social or economic backgrounds.
•	Attract the absolute best students to Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine.

At the core of this priority, we want you to be able to choose a career based primarily on your interests, skills and aptitudes rather than financial considerations due to student debt. Because of this, we offer a variety of scholarships, grants and loans to reduce this burden. We award scholarships based on need and merit. Merit-based scholarships look at an accepted applicant's academics. Need-base scholarships are reviewed using parental income and asset data. This is a practice consistent with most medical schools in the country. Tuition and scholarship awards are the same all four years of school.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The Mayo Clinic Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP) is an M.D.-Ph.D. training program that prepares students to translate scientific discoveries into applications that improve patient care. Mayo Clinic MSTP students are able to complete laboratory research rotations and Ph.D. research training at any of the three Mayo campuses — Rochester, Minnesota; Phoenix/Scottsdale, Arizona; and Jacksonville, Florida. Students are able to complete the final two years of medical school at the same campus where they completed the Ph.D. research training.

Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine offers nearly 200 academic enrichment opportunities designed for students to customize their education to meet their individual goals. Options include advanced degrees, clinical electives, global health and research experiences, selectives, and more.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Degree: All applicants must have a bachelor's or Pharm.D. degree from an accredited college or university in the United States or Canada. A higher degree cannot be substituted for this requirement. All degrees must be completed prior to MCASOM orientation.

Prerequisite Coursework: Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine does not require prerequisite college courses for admission. Successful applicants have a broad, strong academic background in life sciences, physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities as reflected in Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) scores. On-line courses accepted. AP and IB accepted if on transcript.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine is dedicated to enrolling students with superior academic credentials and leadership characteristics who have demonstrated a profound commitment to service. A preliminary assessment of academics, degree, and citizenship is performed, and those who meet the minimal expectations will receive a secondary application. After we receive the secondary application, secondary fee or waiver, and the minimum required letters, applications are reviewed through MCASOM's mission aligned selection. This includes GPA and MCAT, demographics, scholarly activity, experiential depth and breadth, essays, and letters. Selected applicants will be offered an interview on a rolling basis until all interview slots are filled. Once interviewed, each applicant is deliberated on and given an admissions committee score. Applicants are offered acceptance based on an assessment of application materials, interview, ranking, and other characteristics they may contribute to the class.
